verdict.rationale: Browserbase advertises full browser control with auto-waits and network interception [docs-4], so a developer driving a session can decide when to extract page content. Its fetch API converts URLs into HTML, JSON or markdown [docs-3], but no documented option controls when that content is returned. Any latency-versus-completeness tradeoff therefore has to be built by the developer in browser automation code, not set through a documented knob. Missing for 10: documented wait or return-timing parameters on the fetch API (e.g. wait-for-selector, wait-until-network-idle, timeouts), guidance on the latency/completeness tradeoff, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
